chunks: We said: The rightful punishments remain in the account of those who deserve them,
if the Imam appears and those who deserve them are still alive, he will enforce them against them based on testimony or confession;
and if this was missed because they died, then the sin of failing to enforce them rests on those who threatened the Imam and forced him into occultation.
And this is not abrogation of the enforcement of punishments,
because a penal code has to be upheld only when there is power and capacity for upholding it and when there is no encumbrance; its enforcement is not binding if there is an encumbrance.
Abrogation is involved when a code is not enforced even when there is power and capacity to enforce it and there is no encumbrance.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam, specifically referring to Imam Mahdi in this context
key_terms.الْحُدُودُ: Divine penal codes or fixed punishments

ai.seo_question: Why are penal codes not enforced during the occultation of Imam Mahdi?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elucidates that the obligation of hudud is suspended rather than abrogated during the Minor and Major Occultations, as the prerequisite of 'ability' (tamkin) is absent. He assigns the sin of non-enforcement to those who obstructed the Imam’s authority, thereby preserving the legal continuity of divine penalties pending the Imam’s reappearance. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that conditions for execution must be fully met, distinguishing between permanent abrogation and temporary suspension due to external impediments.
